header.name: canon
header.role: one memory record, rendered into every tool's own file
header.tagline: Own one region of the file. Leave every byte outside it alone.

flows.kicker: a tool file is somebody's working file first, and canon is a guest in it
flows.title: How one record becomes the file each of your tools reads
flows.footnote: The allow-list and the region are the two rules that make this safe to run against a file you already care about. canon writes four paths and refuses every other one, and inside those four it rewrites only the span between its own markers. A file with no canon region is left exactly as it was, which means opting in is a thing you do to a file rather than a thing canon does to you.
flows.alt: Eight stages taking one record to the file a tool reads: record, validate, layer, resolve, render, region, allow-list, write. Every entry is one envelope in one of five kinds: an authored personality block, an episodic memory, a synthesized persona, a decision record, and a reference to an external research artifact. The validator checks every field and refuses a record it cannot vouch for. A workspace block overrides a global block carrying the same id, and the resolve step keeps current entries only, ordered by a clock-free ordinal so a rebuild is byte-identical. The block set is rendered to text and spliced into the span between the canon begin and end markers, and every byte outside that span is preserved. The write allow-list holds four surfaces: a global and a workspace file for Claude Code, an AGENTS.md for Codex, and a workspace SOUL.md for Hermes. A path outside that list is refused, and so is a file with no canon region. Three outcomes: written inside the markers canon owns, a surface that drifted and needs a human, and a file canon declines to write at all.

flows.kicker: a field that quietly fails to survive the trip is the whole failure mode
flows.title: How a rendered file is checked back against the record it came from
flows.footnote: A round-trip that loses a field is only acceptable when the loss was named first. Each storage adapter declares in advance which fields it cannot carry, the gate classifies every observed loss against that declaration, and a loss nobody declared is a refusal rather than a warning. The aggregate check folds four legs and a leg whose seam is not wired sits out instead of voting a pass it did not earn.
flows.alt: Eight stages checking a rendered file back against its record: read, extract, ingest, canonical, compare, drops, legs, verdict. The file is read as it sits on disk and the region between the canon markers is extracted byte exactly. The region text is ingested back into records, each reduced to one canonical form so the comparison is against a single shape rather than a formatting accident. The rendered form and the ingested form are compared field by field. Every field that failed to survive is classified against the losses that storage adapter declared in advance, and a loss nobody declared is a refusal. The aggregate check folds four legs: surface drift, the vault round-trip, the vault read symmetry, and the persona assessment. A leg whose seam is not wired reports nothing and does not affect the result. The verdict is one exit code, zero when every wired leg passed and one otherwise, and all four gate functions in the codebase share that signature so a build keys on them the same way. Three outcomes: the record survives the file, a declared drop that was named in advance, and a refusal that returns a nonzero code.

cards.title: What canon carries, and where each number is read from
cards.source: src/canon and tests, on this checkout
cards.alt: A table of twelve rows: what canon carries, how many of it there are, and where each number is read from. Five record kinds share one envelope. Two scopes layer, workspace over global. Four surfaces sit on the write allow-list: a global and a workspace file for Claude Code, an AGENTS.md for Codex, and a workspace SOUL.md for Hermes. Four storage adapters implement the backend protocol, and five capability tokens describe what each one can carry. Sixteen schema pins name the seams that carry a version. The aggregate check folds four legs, and four gate functions share the same zero or one exit code. Thirty-four source modules hold five thousand five hundred and sixty-two lines, and thirty-five test files hold six hundred and seventy-six tests. Two surfaces named in the roadmap are absent from the catalog, a global SOUL.md and a GEMINI.md, so canon does not render them.
cards.footnote: Every count here was read from the module that defines it rather than typed in. The marked row is the honest null: the README names a global SOUL.md and a GEMINI.md as later phases, and the write allow-list does not carry them, so those two files are ones canon will not touch today.

fields.note: KINDS in schema.py: personality-block, episodic-memory, synthesized-persona-l3, adr-decision, research-artifact-ref. One envelope shape covers all five.
A global block is the default everywhere. A workspace block carrying the same id overrides it where that workspace applies, and resolve keeps current entries only.
SURFACE_CATALOG in registry.py: a global and a workspace file for Claude Code, an AGENTS.md for Codex, and a workspace SOUL.md for Hermes.
A local file store, a zero-drop SQLite reference, and injected-handle adapters for a memory fact-engine and an authored-block store, all behind one protocol.
relations, temporal, audit-chain, arbitrary-kind and foreign-provenance. An adapter declares what it carries, so a drop is known before a write.
SEAM_PINS in versions.py. Each pin names a seam, its version, and the decision record behind it, so a shape change is a version change.
canon_check folds surface drift, the vault round-trip, the vault read symmetry, and the persona assessment. An unwired leg reports nothing.
drift, reconcile, vault read and the aggregate check each return zero on a clean run and one otherwise, so a build gates on all four the same way.
Python modules under src/canon, including the four backends and the transport seam.
Counted across those modules. No runtime dependencies: the record, the codecs and every gate are standard library only.
pytest over thirty-five files: 543 test functions plus their parametrized cases, covering the record, the backends and every number here.
A global SOUL.md and a GEMINI.md are named in the README as later phases and are absent from the write allow-list, so canon does not write them.
